did_you_know.text: Did you know? The psalm opens with a musical instruction: “For the director of music, with stringed instruments,” indicating that it was intended to be performed with instrumental accompaniment.
Did you know? At the beginning of the psalm appears a threefold request: for grace, blessing, and the shining of God’s face—“May God be gracious to us and bless us; may he make his face shine on us.”
Did you know? The expression “may he make his face shine on us” echoes the wording of the Priestly Blessing in the Book of Numbers: “May the LORD make his face shine on you.”
Did you know? The purpose of the blessing is not merely personal: the psalmist asks that God’s ways be known on earth and that his salvation be revealed among all nations.
Did you know? In this verse, the call “May the peoples praise you” is repeated twice, emphasizing that all nations are called to give thanks to God.
Did you know? The joy of the nations is connected to the fact that the LORD judges the peoples with equity—with fairness and justice—and guides them on earth.
Did you know? The blessing of the land is described in a tangible and simple way: “The land yields its harvest”; the harvest is a visible expression of divine blessing.
Did you know? The psalm’s conclusion extends the blessing to “all the ends of the earth” and presents a connection between God’s blessing and reverence for him.
